docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
This document describes the REST endpoints that external parties can use to connect with UDAP and deliver road user detections.

The Urban Data Access Platform (UDAP) is the national platform in the Netherlands that connects actors in the smart mobility ecosystem. It enables bi-directional, continuous and real-time data exchange, is vendor-independent, and keeps control with the local (city and road) authorities.

The API offers two endpoints:

  • Geofences - Retrieve the list of topologies and their bounding boxes, so that a service provider can determine whether its detection data is relevant to a specific topology
  • Detections - Deliver detection data (location, speed, heading and route) of road users
  • History - Retrieve the processing history of a road user: accepted detections, passages, priority requests and CAMs

docs.title: Target group
docs.text: This document is intended for bike fleet operators and cycling app providers wanting to share the detections of their cyclists with UDAP. It is the technical specification for the connection between their systems and UDAP.

docs.title: Interface flow
docs.text:
1. Retrieve geofences - Retrieve the topologies and their bounding boxes using GET /geofences
  2. Select relevant detections - Use the bounding boxes to determine which detections are relevant to a topology
  3. Post detections - Send the relevant detections using POST /detections
  4. Keep alive - Send an empty array to POST /detections every 30 seconds when there are no valid detections to post
  5. Check history - Optionally retrieve the history of a road user using GET /history/{roadUserId} to see how its detections were processed

See REST API for the details of each endpoint.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
This document uses a versioning scheme that indicates the version of the API specification and tracks the revisions of this document. The scheme is <specification version major>.<specification version minor>.<document revision>.

  • The major version is only bumped when there is a compatibility-breaking change in the specification
  • The minor version is bumped on trivial, non-breaking changes of the specification
  • The document revision is bumped on changes to this document that do not change the specification

The current document version is shown in the footer of every page.

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text: The API is exposed using HTTPS only. SSL (TLS) is used to encrypt all in-flight data.

docs.title: Basic authentication
docs.text:
The API uses HTTP Basic authentication. Every request must include the Authorization header with the base64 encoding of username:password:

Authorization: Basic <base64-encoding of username:password>

docs.title: Obtaining credentials
docs.text:
Credentials are shared separately. You will receive:

  • A username and password for Basic authentication
  • A base URL for the API endpoints; the base URL is specific to each client

docs.title: REST API
docs.text:
All requests and responses use JSON over HTTPS.

All requests require Basic authentication in the Authorization header. See Authentication for details.

The endpoints are relative to the API base URL. The base URL is specific to each client and is shared together with the credentials. The examples on this page use https://dummyhost.udap.nl/v1 as an illustrative base URL.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /geofences Retrieves the list of topologies and their bounding boxes POST /detections Accepts detection data GET /history/{roadUserId} Retrieves the processing history of a road user

docs.title: Compression
docs.text:
Responses (in practice GET /geofences and larger GET /history/{roadUserId} responses) are gzip compressed when the request includes the Accept-Encoding: gzip header and the response is at least 1 KB. A compressed response includes the Content-Encoding: gzip header.

Check every response

Whether a response is compressed differs per request. Clients that send Accept-Encoding: gzip must check every response for the Content-Encoding: gzip header.

docs.title: GET /geofences
docs.text:
Retrieves the list of topologies and their bounding boxes, allowing service providers to determine the relevance of their detection data to a specific topology.

Bounding boxes are a coarse filter

The bounding box only gives a rough indication of the area of a topology. UDAP filters the received detections more precisely, based on the bicycle lanes of the topology. Detections that do not overlap a bicycle lane are counted as detectionsNoOverlap in the history of the road user.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
GET <API base URL>/geofences HTTP/1.1
Host: <hostname>
Authorization: Basic <base64-encoding of username:password>

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

[
  {
    "id": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "referencePoints": [
      {
        "latitude": 0,
        "longitude": 0
      }
    ],
    "boundingBox": {
      "topLeft": {
        "latitude": 0,
        "longitude": 0
      },
      "bottomRight": {
        "latitude": 0,
        "longitude": 0
      }
    }
  }
]
Field Type Required Description id string Yes Identifier for the topology description string No Description for the topology referencePoints array of objects Yes List of intersection reference points; contains at least one reference point referencePoints.latitude double Yes Latitude of a reference point referencePoints.longitude double Yes Longitude of a reference point boundingBox object Yes Bounding box for the topology boundingBox.topLeft object Yes Maximum latitude and minimum longitude (northwest corner) boundingBox.topLeft.latitude double Yes Latitude of the top-left corner of the topology boundingBox.topLeft.longitude double Yes Longitude of the top-left corner of the topology boundingBox.bottomRight object Yes Minimum latitude and maximum longitude (southeast corner) boundingBox.bottomRight.latitude double Yes Latitude of the bottom-right corner of the topology boundingBox.bottomRight.longitude double Yes Longitude of the bottom-right corner of the topology

docs.title: POST /detections
docs.text:
Accepts detection data and keep-alive payloads (an empty array).

Keep-alive

Send a payload with an empty array ([]) every 30 seconds if there are no valid detections to post. The 30-second interval applies per client connection, not per road user: any posted detections reset it.

The keep-alive is used for monitoring only: it lets us detect whether a client is still alive. A missed keep-alive has no other effect.

Request size limit

The request body must not exceed 60 KB.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
POST <API base URL>/detections HTTP/1.1
Host: <hostname>
Authorization: Basic <base64-encoding of username:password>

[
  {
    "roadUserId": "string",
    "detectionTime": "2025-01-29T12:00:00Z",
    "detection": {
      "latitude": 0,
      "longitude": 0,
      "speed": 0,
      "heading": 0,
      "accuracy": 0
    },
    "route": [
      {
        "latitude": 0,
        "longitude": 0
      }
    ]
  }
]
Field Type Required Description roadUserId string Yes Unique identifier of a road user (cyclist or bike) detectionTime string Yes Time of the detection, ISO 8601 formatted in UTC (e.g. 2025-01-29T12:00:00Z) detection object Yes Location and movement of the road user at the time of the detection detection.latitude double Yes Latitude of the detected road user's location detection.longitude double Yes Longitude of the detected road user's location detection.speed double No (nullable) Speed of the road user in meters per second detection.heading double No (nullable) Direction the road user is moving in (0-360°, 0° is north, clockwise) detection.accuracy integer Yes Accuracy of the location detection in meters route array of objects No (nullable) Array of waypoints. No route (null or an empty array) means that the road user has reached their destination route.latitude double Yes Latitude of a waypoint along the route route.longitude double Yes Longitude of a waypoint along the route

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK

A successful request returns no response body.

docs.title: GET /history/{roadUserId}
docs.text:
Retrieves the processing history of a road user: how many of its detections were received and accepted, and which traffic light controllers it passed, including the priority requests and CAMs that UDAP sent on its behalf.

History is built periodically

The history is rebuilt every minute. Changes take about 3 minutes to become visible. Until the first history of a road user has been built, the endpoint returns 404 Not Found.

The history covers the activity of the road user in the 24 hours before the history was built.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
GET <API base URL>/history/{roadUserId} HTTP/1.1
Host: <hostname>
Authorization: Basic <base64-encoding of username:password>
Parameter Description roadUserId The roadUserId used in POST /detections, URL-encoded

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "asOf": "string",
  "window": {
    "from": "string",
    "to": "string"
  },
  "summary": {
    "detectionsReceived": 0,
    "detectionsRejected": 0,
    "detectionsNoOverlap": 0
  },
  "passages": [
    {
      "tlc": "string",
      "enteredAt": "string",
      "exitedAt": "string",
      "camsPublished": 0,
      "srm0": [
        {
          "sentAt": "string",
          "connections": [
            {
              "intersectionId": 0,
              "laneConnectionId": 0
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "roadUserId": "string",
  "lastEventProcessed": "string"
}

All timestamps are ISO 8601 formatted in UTC.

Field Type Required Description asOf string Yes Time the history was built window object Yes Period covered by the history window.from string Yes Start of the period: 24 hours before window.to window.to string Yes End of the period summary object Yes Detection counts for the period summary.detectionsReceived integer Yes Number of detections received for the road user summary.detectionsRejected integer Yes Number of detections rejected because they failed validation (for example a missing field or an invalid format) summary.detectionsNoOverlap integer Yes Number of detections that did not overlap a bicycle lane passages array of objects Yes Passages of the road user through a topology passages.tlc string Yes Traffic light controller passed; matches the id from GET /geofences passages.enteredAt string Yes Time the road user entered the topology passages.exitedAt string No (nullable) Time of the last detection in the topology. null while the passage is ongoing; a passage ends when no detection is received for 30 seconds passages.camsPublished integer Yes Number of Cooperative Awareness Messages (CAMs) published for the road user during the passage passages.srm0 array of objects Yes Soft priority requests (SRMs) sent on behalf of the road user passages.srm0.sentAt string Yes Time the priority request was sent passages.srm0.connections array of objects Yes Lane connections for which priority was requested passages.srm0.connections.intersectionId integer Yes Identifier of the intersection passages.srm0.connections.laneConnectionId integer Yes Identifier of the lane connection on the intersection roadUserId string Yes Identifier of the road user lastEventProcessed string Yes Time of the last detection received from the road user

If there is no history for the road user (yet), the response is:

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json
